_notes: Parts pulled from 3 Amazon orders placed 2026-09-15. Amazon product pages weren't reachable directly, so specs come from manufacturer/reseller pages for the same generic part. 'source_url' is where the bulk of the specs came from; 'other_sources' backs up specific numbers. Fields marked 'unverified' or 'caveat' are worth checking against the physical part.

items.type: motor (DC gear motor with integrated encoder)
items.exact_name_on_invoice: High Torque Gear Motor JGB37-520 Encoder Motor, Smart Car Motor DC12V Small Car Plane Model Engine Kit, Low Speed Geared Motor (Color: 12v, Size: 330RPM)

specs.motor_type: brushed DC, metal spur reduction gearbox, reversible
specs.speed_variant: listed as 330RPM; reference tables list this ratio as 319 RPM (18.8:1); some sellers call it 333 RPM and quote 1:30 ratio. Treat true ratio as UNVERIFIED - measure encoder counts per output rev to confirm
specs.gear_ratio: 18.8:1 per rcdrone table (most likely); 1:30 per some resellers
specs.stall_torque: 1.9 kgf·cm (~0.186 N·m)  [colgroad lists max torque 1.5 kg·cm]

dimensions.mounting: 6x M3 threaded holes on 31 mm pitch circle, ~3.5-4 mm deep

specs.output_shaft: 6 mm D-shaft, 15.5 mm long, flat length 12 mm, 5.5 mm across flat; 12 mm dia x 6 mm locating boss

encoder.base_resolution: 11 PPR at motor shaft (22-pole magnet ring). Output-shaft counts = 11 x gear ratio (≈207 PPR at 18.8:1, ≈330 PPR at 30:1), x4 with full quadrature decoding (≈827 CPR at 18.8:1)

wiring.red: motor power + (swap with white to reverse)

specs.caveat: Do not put 12V on encoder VCC. All figures are supplier reference data.

items.exact_name_on_invoice: GY-91 10DOF Sensor Module MPU9250 for bmp280 IIC for spi GY-91

specs.chips: InvenSense MPU-9250 (3-axis accel + 3-axis gyro + AK8963 3-axis magnetometer) + Bosch BMP280 (pressure + temperature)
specs.module_size: 14.3 x 20.5 mm (some listings say 23 x 18 x 5 mm)
specs.pins: VIN, 3V3, GND, SCL, SDA, SDO/SAO, NCS (MPU-9250 SPI chip select), CSB (BMP280 SPI chip select)
specs.default_i2c_addresses: MPU-9250: 0x68 (0x69 if AD0 high); AK8963 mag: 0x0C (reachable via MPU bypass mode); BMP280: 0x76 or 0x77 [from chip datasheets, not the listing]
specs.caveat: MPU-9250 is discontinued; many cheap GY-91 boards ship an MPU-6500 (no magnetometer). Check WHO_AM_I register: 0x71 = MPU-9250, 0x70 = MPU-6500. [general knowledge, not from listing]

items.exact_name_on_invoice: ideaspark ESP32 Development Board Integrated 0.96 Inch OLED Display, CH340 Driver, WiFi+BLE Wireless Module, and Micro USB Works Great for Arduino/Micropython (Pin Header Soldered)

specs.cpu: dual-core Xtensa LX6, up to 240 MHz
specs.layout: same peripheral pinout as ESP32 DevKit V1 (30-pin), with OLED added
specs.oled: 0.96 inch, 128x64, SSD1306 controller, two-tone (yellow top band / blue)
specs.oled_i2c_pins: SDA = GPIO21, SCL = GPIO22 (per listing). Note espboards.dev shows a different board variant using SDA=GPIO4/SCL=GPIO15/RST=GPIO16; if the display doesn't respond, try those
specs.power_input: 5V via USB or VIN pin; 3V3 pin out
specs.adc: 12-bit SAR; ADC2 pins unusable while Wi-Fi is on
specs.strapping_pins: GPIO0, 2, 5, 12, 15 (avoid pulling these at boot); GPIO34-39 input only; GPIO6-11 tied to flash
specs.caveat: Since the OLED shares the I2C bus on GPIO21/22, the GY-91 can sit on the same bus (different addresses).

items.exact_name_on_invoice: Shutao 2 Pcs TB6612FNG DC Motor Drive Module 1.2A Peak 3.2A Compatible with DRV8833 Better Than L298N

specs.peak_current: 2 A continuous pulse / 3.2 A single pulse per channel
specs.control_modes: CW, CCW, short brake, stop (via IN1/IN2 + PWM)
specs.standby: STBY pin must be HIGH to enable outputs
specs.pins: VM, VCC, GND, AO1, AO2, BO1, BO2, PWMA, AIN1, AIN2, STBY, BIN1, BIN2, PWMB
specs.fit_with_motors: JGB37-520 stall current is ~1.2 A @ 12V, which is right at the 1.2 A continuous limit and well under the 3.2 A peak - OK, but avoid sustained stalls. 12V on VM is within limits; 2S Li-ion (8.4V max) is also fine.

items.exact_name_on_invoice: SOVNSG LM2596 DC-DC Buck Converter, 10pcs, 3.2V-35V to 1.25V-35V

specs.input_voltage: 3.2-35V (some listings say up to 40V; don't exceed 35V)
specs.output_voltage: 1.25-35V adjustable via multi-turn trimpot; must be ~1.5V+ below input
specs.output_current: 3 A max; ~2 A continuous without heatsink
specs.efficiency: up to ~92% (lower at low Vout; ~73% at 12V->3V 3A per one datasheet)
specs.caveat: Ships at an arbitrary output voltage - set it with a multimeter BEFORE connecting the ESP32. Turn trimpot counterclockwise to lower output.

items.exact_name_on_invoice: Yuntunele 2Pack 18650 Batteries 3.7V 3500mAh Button Top Rechargeable Battery, 3500mah 3.7v 12.95wh Rechargeable Batteries, for LED Flashlight, Headlamps, Doorbells, RC Cars

specs.protection: listing claims 'six layers of safety protection' - likely a protection circuit, not confirmed
specs.size: ~65 x 18 mm (2.56 x 0.71 in); button-top cells run a few mm longer than flat-top
specs.pack_config_in_project: 2 cells in series in the ACEIRMC holder = 7.4V nominal, 8.4V full, ~6V empty
specs.caveat: Off-brand capacity claims are often inflated; one buyer measured ~1.8-2.1 Ah per cell. No continuous discharge rating given - two JGB37 motors near stall (~2.4 A total) could be a stretch. Budget for ~2000 mAh real capacity.

items.exact_name_on_invoice: ACEIRMC 2pcs 18650 Battery Storage Case 2 Slots x 3.7V for 2x18650 Batteries Holder Box Container with ON/Off Switch (2 Slots with Switch Cover)

specs.cover: sliding cover secured with small screw
specs.caveat: A buyer reported poor contact with flat-top cells; your Yuntunele cells are button-top, so should be fine. 7.4V nominal is below the motors' 12V rating, so expect roughly 60-70% of rated speed (~190-220 RPM no-load) unless you add a boost converter.

items.exact_name_on_invoice: Ferwooh 10pcs PCB Board Prototype Kit Protoboard Circuit Board Breadboards 432 Holes Perfboard Universal Printed Circuit Breadboard for DIY Soldering Electronic Projects and Electronic Experiment

system_level_notes.power_tree_suggestion: 2S 18650 pack (6-8.4V) -> TB6612FNG VM directly; same pack -> LM2596 set to 5V -> ESP32 VIN; ESP32 3V3 -> GY-91 VIN and TB6612 VCC
system_level_notes.i2c_bus: ESP32 GPIO21/22 shared by OLED (0x3C), MPU-9250 (0x68), BMP280 (0x76/0x77)
system_level_notes.encoder_pins: 4 encoder signals (2 per motor) need interrupt-capable GPIOs; ESP32 PCNT peripheral can count quadrature in hardware
system_level_notes.voltage_mismatch: Motors are 12V-rated but the battery pack is 7.4V nominal - top speed and torque will be lower than the spec table
